description: Airflow errors learned from this platform's own failures (Airflow task logs, incidents and Datadog), one entry per error shape no shipped runbook covers. Built by infrastructure/build_airflow_error_pack.py and seeded with airflow_runbook_pack.json; review the entries before deploying.

knowledge.title: SnapLogic gate stopped the DAG (snaplogic_end: trigger_snaplogic did not succeed)
knowledge.content: Signals: 'AirflowException: trigger_snaplogic did not succeed -- hard-stopping dbt via snaplogic_end'. Meaning: snaplogic_end is a guard task. It fails on purpose when trigger_snaplogic did not succeed (or did not push its snaplogic_details XCom), so the dbt tasks do not run on a partial load. It is never the root cause. Usual causes: the SnapLogic pipeline itself failed: a rejected bearer token (401 'Mismatched bearer token'), an Exit snap threshold exceeded by error documents, a Snaplex outage, or trigger_snaplogic killed before it wrote its XCom. Repair: open trigger_snaplogic in the same run and read its error (it names the SnapLogic runtime id, ruuid); repair that with its own runbook; then clear trigger_snaplogic with downstream so snaplogic_end and dbt run again. Rerunning snaplogic_end alone fails again.

content_json.meaning: A guard task stopped the DAG because the SnapLogic trigger task did not succeed; the cause is in trigger_snaplogic.
content_json.usual_cause: SnapLogic pipeline failure: rejected bearer token, Exit snap threshold exceeded, Snaplex outage, or the trigger task killed before writing its XCom.
human_steps: Open trigger_snaplogic in the same DAG run and read its error and the SnapLogic runtime id (ruuid).
Fix the SnapLogic failure with its own runbook (bearer token, Exit threshold, Snaplex).
Clear trigger_snaplogic with downstream so snaplogic_end and the dbt tasks rerun; do not rerun snaplogic_end alone.

knowledge.title: Post-MDM to gold: upstream engine DAG failed, not publishing to Kafka
knowledge.content: Signals: 'AirflowFailException: [post-mdm-property] (or [post-mdm-company]) gdp_engine_<entity>_incremental_<env> FAILED for run ...; not publishing to Kafka'. Meaning: the gdp_post_mdm_to_gold_<entity> DAG waits (wait_es_sync) for the engine DAG's es_sync_done event for the same run. The engine DAG failed, so the wait task fails fast and nothing is published to Kafka. Usual causes: the engine DAG's Kubernetes task (sync to OpenSearch) failed: container exit, pod not found during cleanup, pod unschedulable, or a dbt failure in the gold OpenSearch models. Repair: open the engine DAG run named in the message and fix it first (see the Kubernetes and dbt runbooks). Once that run succeeds, clear wait_es_sync with downstream in the post-MDM DAG. Do not mark wait_es_sync success by hand: Kafka would get events for data that was not synced.

content_json.meaning: The post-MDM DAG stopped because the upstream engine DAG failed for the same run.
content_json.usual_cause: A failure in gdp_engine_<entity>_incremental_<env>: Kubernetes sync task or gold dbt models.
human_steps: Open the engine DAG run named in the message and find its failed task.
Fix and rerun the engine DAG until it succeeds.
Clear wait_es_sync with downstream in the post-MDM DAG; never mark it success by hand.

knowledge.title: pipeline_done: pipeline marked FAILED in GDP_BATCH_MASTER (a stage failed earlier)
knowledge.content: Signals: 'ValueError: [pipeline-done] Pipeline marked FAILED in GDP_BATCH_MASTER (overall_status=FAILED; stage failures: SnapLogic=FAILED | dbt (silver)=FAILED)', 'Failing this task to ensure the DAG run state is FAILED in the Airflow UI'. Meaning: pipeline_done is the summary task of the GDP ingestion DAGs. It reads the batch's stage results from GDP_BATCH_MASTER and fails on purpose so the DAG run shows FAILED. The ValueError is not a code bug. Usual causes: an earlier stage failed; the message names it (SnapLogic=FAILED: see the SnapLogic gate and SnapLogic runbooks; dbt (silver)=FAILED: see the dbt task's log, often a transient Snowflake error or a lock on a shared silver table). Repair: find the failed stage task in the same run, fix it with its own runbook, then clear that stage task with downstream; pipeline_done reruns and passes once GDP_BATCH_MASTER shows the stage succeeded.

signals: Failing this task to ensure the DAG run state is FAILED
content_json.meaning: The DAG's summary task failed on purpose because an earlier stage (SnapLogic or dbt) failed for this batch.
content_json.usual_cause: A failed SnapLogic or dbt (silver) stage, named in 'stage failures:'.
human_steps: Read 'stage failures:' in the message to find the failed stage.
Open that stage's task in the same run and fix it with its own runbook.
Clear the failed stage task with downstream; pipeline_done reruns after it.

knowledge.title: Kubernetes pod container failed (sync-property-es exit code 1)
knowledge.content: Signals: "'message': 'sync-property-es: failed'", "'terminated': {'container_id'", "'exit_code': 1", pod phase Failed. Meaning: the container that syncs property documents to OpenSearch (gdp_engine_property_incremental_<env>) exited with an error. Airflow only sees the pod status. Usual causes: the sync job failed on OpenSearch (cluster unavailable, index mapping rejected a document, bulk request rejected, credentials), on its Snowflake read, or ran much longer than usual and was stopped. Repair: read the container's own log (the pod log in the task log, or Datadog for the pod name), fix what it reports, then rerun the task. A rerun alone is reasonable when the log shows an OpenSearch or network timeout.

content_json.meaning: The OpenSearch sync container in the Kubernetes pod exited with an error.
content_json.usual_cause: OpenSearch unavailable or rejecting documents, a Snowflake read failure, or a run far longer than usual.
human_steps: Read the container log of the pod (task log or Datadog by pod name).
Check OpenSearch cluster health and index mapping errors.
Rerun the task after the fix; one rerun is fine for a timeout.

knowledge.title: SnapLogic trigger rejected: 401 Mismatched bearer token
knowledge.content: Signals: 'Exception: SnapLogic trigger HTTPError 401 UNAUTHORIZED', '"message": "Mismatched bearer token"'. Meaning: the SnapLogic triggered task refused the bearer token the DAG sent. Usual causes: the triggered task was recreated or its token regenerated in SnapLogic, while the Airflow connection or the Akeyless secret (under the environment's AKEYLESS_BASE_PATH) still holds the old one; or the DAG points at another environment's task URL. Repair: a human step. In SnapLogic Manager open the triggered task, copy its current bearer token, update the Airflow connection or Akeyless secret for this environment, then clear trigger_snaplogic with downstream. Retries do not help: every try fails the same way.

content_json.meaning: SnapLogic rejected the triggered task's bearer token.
content_json.usual_cause: Token regenerated or task recreated in SnapLogic without updating the Airflow connection / Akeyless secret, or a URL for another environment.
human_steps: Open the triggered task in SnapLogic Manager and copy its bearer token.
Update the Airflow connection or the Akeyless secret under this environment's AKEYLESS_BASE_PATH.
Clear trigger_snaplogic with downstream.

knowledge.title: Snowflake 210012: Failed to copy previous results (dbt execute_via_snowflake)
knowledge.content: Signals: '210012 (P0000): Failed to copy previous results', 'Database Error in model execute_via_snowflake', 'dbt-ol run --select tag:<source>_company_silver ... failed'. Meaning: Snowflake failed internally while reusing a previous query result during the dbt run. The SQL and the data are fine. Usual causes: a transient Snowflake service error, most often when many silver dbt runs (company_merged_pipeline) start at the same time. Repair: one rerun (RERUN_ONLY) of the dbt task normally passes. When it recurs, add retries to the dbt profile (retries: 2) or the task (retries with retry_exponential_backoff), disable result reuse in execute_via_snowflake with a pre_hook 'ALTER SESSION SET USE_CACHED_RESULT = FALSE', stagger the source DAGs, and open a Snowflake support case with the query id.

content_json.meaning: A transient Snowflake internal error while reusing a previous query result.
content_json.usual_cause: Snowflake service error, often when many silver dbt runs start together.
human_steps: Rerun the failed dbt task.
When it recurs, add dbt or Airflow retries with backoff and USE_CACHED_RESULT = FALSE in execute_via_snowflake.
Open a Snowflake support case with the query id.

knowledge.title: Kubernetes pod not found (ApiException 404) while Airflow reads or cleans up the pod
knowledge.content: Signals: 'ApiException: (404)', '"reason":"NotFound"', '"kind":"pods"'. Meaning: the KubernetesPodOperator asked for its pod's status or logs and the pod was already gone. Usual causes: the node was scaled in or the pod evicted, a retry of the same task deleted the earlier pod, or the pod was cleaned up before Airflow read it. Repair: one rerun (RERUN_ONLY) usually passes. When it recurs, check the cluster events and the autoscaler around the failure time, use on_finish_action='delete_succeeded_pod' so failed pods stay for inspection, and give the task retries with backoff.

content_json.meaning: Airflow could not find the task's Kubernetes pod.
content_json.usual_cause: Node scale-in or eviction, a retry deleting the earlier pod, or early cleanup.
human_steps: Rerun the task.
Check cluster events and the autoscaler at the failure time.
Set on_finish_action='delete_succeeded_pod' and retries with backoff.

knowledge.title: SnapLogic Exit snap: exceeded threshold limit (error documents in the pipeline)
knowledge.content: Signals: "SnapLogic run for <SOURCE> failed: Snap 'Exit': Exceeded threshold limit -- Number of input documents received is more than 0". Meaning: the pipeline's Exit snap is a data check. It stops the pipeline when any document reaches the error path. Records failed validation or mapping inside SnapLogic. Usual causes: new or malformed values from the source (a new code, a null in a required field, a changed file layout), or a mapping change in the pipeline. Repair: a human step. Open the runtime by its ruuid in SnapLogic Manager and read the documents in the error view; fix the source data or the pipeline mapping; then clear trigger_snaplogic with downstream. Rerunning without a fix fails the same way.

signals: Number of input documents received is more than
content_json.meaning: Documents reached the SnapLogic pipeline's error path and its Exit snap stopped it.
content_json.usual_cause: New or malformed source values or a pipeline mapping change.
human_steps: Open the runtime (ruuid in the message) in SnapLogic Manager and read the error view documents.
Fix the source data or the pipeline mapping; tell the source owner when the source changed.
Clear trigger_snaplogic with downstream.

knowledge.title: DBT job failed: duplicate row detected during DML (100090) in a gold model
knowledge.content: Signals: 'DBT job failed: N model(s) failed out of N total', 'Duplicate row detected during DML action' (100090), first error in a gold model such as property_es_doc. Meaning: the model's MERGE matched one target row with several source rows. Usual causes: a join in the model fans out (several MDM matches or history rows per key), or an upstream silver table received the same record twice. Repair: find the duplicate keys in the model's source query (GROUP BY key HAVING COUNT(*) > 1). A fan-out is fixed in the model (QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY key ...) = 1 or a tighter join), a code change; duplicates in an upstream table follow the duplicate-keys runbook. Rerun the engine DAG after.

signals: Duplicate row detected during DML action
content_json.meaning: A gold dbt model's MERGE found several source rows for one key.
content_json.usual_cause: A fan-out join in the model or duplicates in an upstream silver table.
human_steps: Find the duplicate keys in the model's source query.
Deduplicate in the model (QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() = 1) or fix the join.
Rerun the engine DAG.

knowledge.title: dbt property_event_outbox: STAGE.EVENT_OUTBOX_PROPERTY does not exist or not authorized (002003)
knowledge.content: Signals: '002003 (42S02): SQL compilation error', "Object '<ENV>_GDP_SILVER_DB.STAGE.EVENT_OUTBOX_PROPERTY' does not exist or not authorized", 'Database Error in model property_event_outbox'. Meaning: the post-MDM dbt model that writes the Kafka event outbox cannot see its STAGE table. Usual causes: the table was not deployed in this environment yet, or the environment's data engineer role has no privilege on the STAGE schema (new table without future grants). Repair: a human step. Check the table exists (SHOW TABLES LIKE 'EVENT_OUTBOX_PROPERTY' IN SCHEMA <ENV>_GDP_SILVER_DB.STAGE); deploy it when missing, or grant the role SELECT/INSERT on it and future grants on the schema. Rerun the post-MDM DAG after.

signals: does not exist or not authorized
content_json.meaning: The event outbox model cannot see its STAGE table.
content_json.usual_cause: Table not deployed in this environment or missing grants for the environment role.
human_steps: Check the table exists in <ENV>_GDP_SILVER_DB.STAGE.
Deploy it or grant the environment role privileges and future grants.
Rerun the post-MDM DAG.

knowledge.title: Kubernetes pod could not start (nodes available: Insufficient memory, image pull)
knowledge.content: Signals: '0/N nodes are available', 'Insufficient memory', 'Insufficient cpu', 'ErrImagePull', 'ImagePullBackOff'. Meaning: the task's pod never started: no node had the CPU or memory it requests, or the image could not be pulled. Usual causes: the cluster was full or the autoscaler at its maximum, pod requests larger than any node, a wrong image tag after a release, or registry credentials that expired. Repair: a human step for the image (fix the tag or the pull secret). For capacity, rerun when the cluster has room (RERUN_ONLY), and if it recurs lower the pod's requests or raise the node group's capacity.

content_json.meaning: The task's pod could not be scheduled or its image pulled.
content_json.usual_cause: Cluster capacity, oversized requests, wrong image tag or expired pull secret.
human_steps: Check whether the error is capacity (Insufficient) or image (ErrImagePull).
Fix the image tag or pull secret for an image error.
For capacity, rerun later and review requests and node group limits.

knowledge.title: Snowflake lock queue on a shared silver table (has locked table ... not yet released)
knowledge.content: Signals: "Statement '<id>' has locked table '<TABLE>' in transaction <n> and this lock has not yet been released", the dbt model aborted (for example company_core). Meaning: too many statements were already waiting for the lock on the same table, so Snowflake aborted this one. Usual causes: several source DAGs (gdp_<source>_qa with tag company_merged_pipeline) write to the same shared silver table (COMPANY_CORE) at the same time. Repair: one rerun (RERUN_ONLY) once the other runs finish usually passes. When it recurs, run the writers one at a time: an Airflow pool with one slot for the company_merged_pipeline dbt tasks, staggered schedules, or one merge step that the sources feed instead of each writing the table.

signals: lock has not yet been released
content_json.meaning: The statement was aborted while waiting for a lock other runs held on a shared table.
content_json.usual_cause: Concurrent source DAGs writing the same silver table.
human_steps: Check which DAGs were writing the table at the time.
Rerun after they finish.
Serialize the writers with a one-slot Airflow pool or staggered schedules.
